text:
sam.sdk: FYI I'm seeing flaky failures running our Python SDK samples on Windows with CPython 3.8/3.9. Errors look like TLS verify failures or failures loading CA bundle when using the AsyncClient + aiohttp. Anyone hit this across older interpreters?

taylor: Pretty sure 3.8/3.9 on Windows sometimes ship without certifi and rely on the OS store which can be inconsistent in some Docker/image setups. What's the exact error text?

sam.sdk: Example from CI run:
```
aiohttp.client_exceptions.ClientConnectorCertificateError: Cannot connect: ('x.x.x.x', 443) - [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1125)
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File "site-packages/redwood_sdk/retries.py", line 56, in _with_retries
    return await func()
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable
```
Looks like our retry wrapper returns None in some error paths which then breaks code that assumes a Response.

olga: That's two issues in one: (A) cert verification on Windows for older pythons, (B) retry wrapper not preserving exceptions. For (A) maybe we should vendor a fallback to certifi in the client bootstrap if we detect Windows and ssl.get_default_verify_paths().cafile is None.

andy: Agreed. Another quick workaround for users: `python -m pip install certifi` then set `set SSL_CERT_FILE=%PYTHONHOME%\Lib\site-packages\certifi\cacert.pem` before running. Not great but helps in the short term.

taylor: Also note the embeddable Python distribution behaves differently (no cert store). We should document that in docs/onboarding/windows.md and add a sample script in examples/windows to set SSL_CERT_FILE automatically when missing.

sam.sdk: I can add a tiny check in examples: if os.name == 'nt' and not os.environ.get('SSL_CERT_FILE'): try import certifi; os.environ['SSL_CERT_FILE']=certifi.where() 

olga: For the retry bug, we'll need to ensure our async retry returns/raises consistently. I found a race where an exception path swallowed the aiohttp.ClientResponse and returned None; caller iterates headers -> crashes. I'll open a fix.

andy: How about typing support? Users on py3.8 reported no proper AsyncClient type hints in the package which makes autocomplete terrible. The generated stubs currently only cover sync.

taylor: We should ship a py.typed and add explicit AsyncClient definitions in a .pyi so 3rd-party IDEs pick it up for all supported pythons. Also add Mypy CI on 3.8/3.9 to ensure stub compatibility.

sam.sdk: Filing an issue with repro and attaching a small Dockerfile + Windows runner notes. Will include a tiny sample script that demonstrates the env workaround.

ci-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2401 - "windows: cert bundle missing on 3.8/3.9 in some images + async retry None path"

olga: I'll take the retry fix (PR coming). Plan: make retry always raise a unified RedwoodNetworkError on unrecoverable errors and ensure callers don't assume presence of headers. Add unit test simulating aiohttp raising ClientConnectorError and ensure we handle it.

andy: I'll draft the certifi fallback PR: detect Windows or missing cafile and call `context.load_verify_locations(certifi.where())` for both sync and async clients. Add tests on AppVeyor or Windows GH Actions matrix.

taylor: I'll do the typing PR and add a `py.typed` marker + minimal AsyncClient.pyi. Also add docs note in onboarding and examples.

sam.sdk: Thanks. For now I'll update our internal onboarding doc to include the `SSL_CERT_FILE` env workaround so new hires don't hit this.

devex-bot: Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2412 (retry fix), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2415 (certifi fallback), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2419 (typing + py.typed)

sam.sdk: Closing loop here. Once PRs land can we cut a patch release and update examples? We have customers on older Windows runtimes.

olga: We'll aim for patch within the week after CI passes. Thanks for the repro, @sam.sdk :thumbsup:
